unit.title: How agents work: the loop, tools and memory

lesson.title: Teaching it a new tool
lesson.subtitle: Fine-tuning on the phone, what it forgets, and when it’s worth it

video.title: Teaching it a new tool
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Dr Farah Rahman — university lecturer in education, Bangladesh (main character)
Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (cameo)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: A list: A bus question; The glossary?!; Teach it?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Our school wants the agent to answer bus questions. But Darsi Tiny has never heard of a bus tool. Ask when the next bus leaves Kafi, and it looks Kafi up in the glossary! Can we teach it?

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: teaching an agent a new tool, and what it forgets.

scenes.visual: A list: A clearer instruction; Describe a new tool; Change the model: fine-tuning.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Three ways to change an agent
scenes.narration: There are three ways to change what an agent does. Write a clearer instruction. Describe a new tool, which big models can often use. Or change the model itself, from examples: that’s fine-tuning.

scenes.visual: A list: New examples; Its numbers shift; On the phone: top layer, 16 examples, 15 steps.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Fine-tuning means training a model a little more, on new examples. Its numbers shift until its answers match the examples. On your phone, only Darsi Tiny’s top layer learns, from sixteen conversations, in fifteen steps.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the lab, we teach it a bus tool, in English and Arabic. Before, it got none of eight bus questions right. After, seven of eight, even for villages it never saw.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Then we tested its old skills: weather, routes, sums. Before teaching, eight of eight. After, with only new examples, one of eight. It learned the bus, and forgot nearly everything else.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! It learned the bus tool, but forgot the weather. What would you mix into the training?

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Some old conversations. Practising old skills alongside the new one keeps them. With sixteen mixed in, old skills come back to five of eight, and with forty-eight, all eight. But the bus drops to five of eight: there’s always a trade-off.

scenes.visual: A list: Laptop: 38 s to 2 min 16 s; Old phone: about 3 to 11 min; It can change refusals too; Test old skills and safety.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Fine-tuning takes time: on a laptop, from under a minute to over two; on an old phone, about three to eleven minutes. And it can change behaviour you didn’t aim at, even refusals. So test again, every time.

scenes.visual: A list: First: a clearer instruction; Then: a tool, with a check; Last: fine-tune, with a test set.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So when should you fine-tune? Try a clearer instruction first, then a tool with a check in code. Fine-tune only with good examples, a test set for old and new skills, and someone to check it.

scenes.visual: A list: Ask about a bus; Teach: 48 mixed in; Test new and old; Again, with none.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: teach the agent a new tool
scenes.narration: In the app, ask about a bus first. Teach it with forty-eight old conversations mixed in, then test it. Then teach it again with none, and test the old skills.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A colleague fine-tunes the agent on her own examples, and the new answers look great. What should she do before the class uses it?

scenes.visual: Summary points: Fine-tuning learns from examples; It can forget: mix old in; Test old and new, every time.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Fine-tuning learns from examples · It can forget: mix old in · Test old and new, every time
scenes.narration: Test old skills and safety too, before anyone relies on it. Remember: fine-tuning changes a model’s numbers from examples. It can forget what it knew, so mix old examples in. And test both, every time.

scenes.visual: A list: A new signal for quiet; Test the old signals too; Once with practice, once without; Which way forgot?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: teach a new hand signal for quiet, then test the old signals too. Do it once with practice of the old ones, and once without. Which way did the class forget?

checkpoints.prompt: It learned the bus tool, but forgot the weather. What would you mix into the training?

options.text: Some old conversations it already knew

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — practising old conversations alongside the new examples keeps the old skills: with 48 mixed in, all 8 came back.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — more bus examples or longer training don’t bring old skills back. Mix old conversations in.

checkpoints.prompt: A colleague fine-tunes the agent on her own examples, and the new answers look great. What should she do before the class uses it?

options.text: Use it: the new answers look great
Test its old skills and its safety too

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — fine-tuning can quietly break old skills and refusals. Test old and new, and the safety checks, before anyone relies on it.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — great new answers say nothing about the old skills or the refusals. Test those first.
